title: Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards
statement:
A row of `n` cards lies on a table. Card `i` is worth `points[i]` (a value that can be negative). You must take exactly `k` cards, one per move. On every move you may take either the **leftmost** or the **rightmost** card still in the row.

Your score is the sum of the values of the `k` cards you took. Print the maximum score you can reach.

Equivalently, you choose some number `j` of cards from the left end and `k - j` cards from the right end, for any `j` from `0` to `k`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `k`.
The second line contains `n` integers: `points[0] ... points[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the maximum total value of the `k` cards.

examples.explanation: Take the three rightmost cards: `9 + 3 + 5 = 17`. Mixed choices such as `4 + 3 + 5 = 12` or `4 + 1 + 5 = 10` are worse, and the three leftmost give 7.
With k = n you must take every card, so the score is `5 - 2 - 3 + 6 = 6`.
All values are negative. The best pair is `-1` from the left and `-4` from the right, for a total of -5.

hints: If you take `j` cards from the left, you automatically take `k - j` from the right. There are only `k + 1` choices for `j`.
Start with the sum of the first `k` cards (j = k). Then move one card at a time: drop the last left card, add the next card from the right end.
Alternatively, the cards you do not take form one contiguous window of length `n - k`: minimise its sum with a sliding window and subtract from the total.
